name: Haiku-Depths
geological_features: Shallow global ocean over basalt floor
specific_features: Microbial mats that form geometric patterns visible from orbit
Water chemistry that shifts color with seasonal temperature changes
description: Haiku-Depths is a small oceanic world where simplicity belies profundity. Its global ocean averages only three hundred meters in depth, a shallow warm sea spread across a basalt floor pockmarked with hydrothermal mud volcanoes. The low gravity allows the dense atmosphere to hold extraordinary amounts of moisture, creating a perpetual haze that softens the boundary between sea and sky into an indistinct horizon.

The planet's microbial biosphere has achieved something remarkable in its simplicity: vast colonial mats that organize themselves into geometric patterns spanning hundreds of kilometers, visible as precise tessellations from orbit. The patterns shift with the seasons as water chemistry and temperature change, the ocean itself changing color from deep indigo to pale jade in cycles that early cartographers found deeply unsettling in their regularity.

No multicellular life has evolved here despite conditions that seem favorable, a puzzle that has generated dozens of competing hypotheses. The microbial mats dominate every ecological niche so thoroughly that they may actively suppress the emergence of more complex organisms. Some researchers see Haiku-Depths as a world trapped in evolutionary stasis, while others argue it represents an alternative endpoint: life that achieved stability without complexity.

The planet's lithium-rich waters and deuterium concentrations make it economically significant despite its apparent biological simplicity. Extraction operations must navigate strict contamination protocols designed to protect the microbial ecosystems, though enforcement varies with the distance of oversight. Each harvest season, the geometric patterns reform around the extraction platforms, incorporating them into the design as though the mats are writing the intruders into their own inscrutable language.
